newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, no impact from German M3.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, no impact from German M3.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were stable on Wednesday, while the guilder was a touch lower against the German mark with no impact from release of the latest German M3 data, dealers said.

The February M3 figure grew an annualised 8.3 percent compared to the fourth quarter of 1995 versus 8.6 percent in the previous month. The Bundesbank's target range for 1997 M3 money supply growth is 3.5 to 6.5 percent, but dealers said the latest figure was not bad.
The guilder slipped to 112.615 per 100 marks versus 112.595 on Tuesday.
One-year guilder deposits were stable at 3.40 percent bid, which was fractionally higher than its German equivalent.
Up to yesterday, all Dutch deposits were trading at a lower rate than their German equivalents, although the discount has recently narrowed as result of a Dutch rate hike on March 10.
Six-month guilder deposits were bid at the same level as the German equivalent at 3.24 percent.
Other (shorter-dated) guilder rates were trading below German paper.
Dealers said the gap in this segment would narrow should the Dutch central bank raise the special advances rate again, but that this was not likely to happen for some time.
The Dutch special advances, which is roughly comparable to the German repo, is currently pegged at 2.90 percent.
The repo has been fixed at 3.00 percent since August, 1996.
Call money was stable at 3.00 percent, but some dealers said there were only few buyers and they expected call money to slip a little today or on Thursday.
The Dutch central bank will allocate liquidity under a new pact on Friday.
Dealers noted some business in DTCs, the short-term borrowing programmes of the Dutch government, with the focus on the December programme.
The rate for the December programme was set at 3.32 percent this morning and was gradually brought down to 3.29 percent.
